Finance and operations · Practical guide

Four Claude upgrades for clearer finance work

Choose the workflow for a budget, messy export, vendor comparison or contract handoff, and practise on original synthetic files.

Turn a spreadsheet, supplier quote or contract into a structured draft you can check. Start with one plugin that fits today's task; add others only when the next job needs them.

Before you start: Paid Claude access and organisation permission; Claude web or Desktop Chat for the starter route; Original synthetic practice files below.

Choose by the question

  • Finance: variance analysis, reconciliation and accounting drafts. Choose it for clean accounting inputs.
  • Data: CSV/Excel profiling, SQL, charts and dashboards. Choose it before analysis when you need to understand a messy export.
  • Operations: vendor comparisons, process documentation and capacity planning. Ask for assumptions and switching effort alongside price.
  • Legal: clause references, playbook deviations and contract questions for licensed counsel. Use the result as a review handoff.

Add Finance in Claude

  1. Open Customize > Plugins > Discover. Find Finance by Anthropic and choose Add. Expect it to appear among your plugins. If it is missing, check the paid plan and organisation policy.
  2. Start a fresh chat. Type /, or use +, and select the variance-analysis skill. Confirm the workflow is visible before continuing.
  3. Attach the practice CSV and paste the prompt below. No bank, ERP or database connection is needed.

Official plugin help covers web Chat, Desktop Chat and Cowork. Skills and commands work in chat; hooks and sub-agents run in Cowork or Claude Code. Account sync to Code requires a supported current version. Chat access does not imply every plugin component runs there.

Made-up values in illustrative units, created by SkillLantern on 14 November 2026. The repeated E2 row is intentional. These are exercise expectations, not observed plugin results.

Copy this analysis prompt

Check duplicate IDs first. Show repeated rows and deduplicate identical rows only.
From sample.csv calculate budget and actual revenue, expenses and profit
(revenue minus expenses), then show absolute and percentage profit variance.
Keep the arithmetic visible. Explain only what these rows support.
List missing information; do not invent price, volume or business drivers.

Check the answer before trusting the explanation

There are five raw rows, four unique rows and duplicate ID E2. Revenue is 10,000 to 11,000; expenses 6,000 to 6,500; profit 4,000 to 4,500. Profit rises 500 (+12.5%). If the result differs, check duplicate handling and the sign of expenses. These inputs do not establish price or volume drivers.

For a second exercise, download bank.csv and ledger.csv. In a fresh chat choose reconciliation and request unmatched IDs, mismatched amounts and net totals. Expected: T3 differs; bank net 500, ledger net 550; bank minus ledger -50.
